mainTopic: Whether birth-impurity days count toward a זבה's seven clean days, and when blood seen during labor pains makes a woman a זבה
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why the תורה had to teach the count of seven clean days for both a זב and a זבה, since each has its own strictness. אביי then tries to prove that a woman's days of birth-impurity do not count toward a זבה's seven clean days. His first proof, from a ברייתא on "דותה תטמא", is pushed off: "clean" may just mean clean of blood. His second ברייתא compares birth days to נדה days. רבא says it follows רבי אליעזר, and the גמרא asks how one can learn a possible case from an impossible one, which is answered in two ways. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about labor pains. רב חסדא and רבי חנינא argue about a woman whose pains and bleeding both stopped before the birth, and each side defends his view against a challenge from the משנה. רב חסדא explains why רבי מאיר gives both forty and fifty days for early labor pains. Finally, רבי לוי and רב argue about which days the birth keeps her from becoming a זבה, and רב אדא בר אהבה begins a point that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why writing it only for a זב would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה had taught the rule only for a זב, we might have said it does not apply to a זבה, since a זבה is stricter in one way: she becomes טמאה even through אונס.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If the תורה had written it only] with a זב, we would say it applies because he is not made impure by an emission caused by outside circumstances. But a זבה, who is made impure even by circumstances beyond her control, we might say no. So both were necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of why the תורה had to write the rule twice. Writing it only for a זב would leave room to think a זבה is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב is treated more leniently because an emission caused by אונס (outside causes) does not make him טמא. A זבה becomes טמאה even through אונס. So we might have thought the leniency given to a זב does not carry over to her, and that is why it had to be written for her too.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who has an unusual discharge and becomes טמא
A woman who sees blood outside her normal time and becomes טמאה
Circumstances beyond one's control (an emission caused by an outside factor)
It was necessary to teach both cases

phrases.english: [If it had been written only] with a zav — because he is not made impure through circumstances beyond his control,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets fill in the start of the sentence, "if the תורה had written it," which the גמרא leaves out here.

phrases.english: but a zava — who is made impure even through circumstances beyond her control,
I might say no; therefore it was necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a צריכותא that began before this section, explaining why the פסוק mentions both זב and זבה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each case adds something the other could not teach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A leniency taught only for a זב would not apply to a זבה, since she is stricter about אונס.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule had to be written for the זבה as well.

steps.title: Why writing it only for a זבה would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה had taught the rule only for a זבה, we might have said it does not apply to a זב, since a זב is stricter in a different way: three sightings on one day make him טמא, just like sightings on three separate days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Merciful One had written it only with a זבה, we would say it applies because she is not made impure by sightings on one day the way she is by sightings on separate days. But a זב, who is made impure by sightings on one day just as by separate days, we might say no. So both were necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second half of the צריכותא. Writing the rule only for a זבה would leave room to think a זב is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זבה becomes a full זבה only by seeing on three separate days, so three sightings in one day do not count that way for her. A זב becomes a full זב even through three sightings in one day. Each one is stricter in some way, so neither case could be learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Merciful One": the תורה, or ה׳, who wrote it
Sightings, meaning occurrences of a discharge
Like days: sightings on one day counting the same as sightings on separate days

steps.whatToRemember: Both cases had to be written because each has its own strictness. A זבה becomes טמאה through אונס, and a זב becomes טמא through three sightings in one day.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written it with a zava —
because she is not made impure through sightings as through days,
phrases.notes: For her, three sightings on one day are not the same as sightings on three separate days.

phrases.english: but a zav, who is made impure through sightings as through days —
I might say no; therefore it was necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 1, completing the צריכותא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A leniency taught only for a זבה would not apply to a זב, since he is stricter about sightings on one day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule had to be written for the זב as well, so both writings are needed.

steps.title: אביי introduces a ברייתא on "דותה תטמא"
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks what his source is for his earlier ruling and begins quoting a ברייתא. Its first teaching is that the man who has relations with her is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: From where do I say this? As it is taught: "Her sickness she shall be impure" comes to include the man who has relations with her.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins bringing a proof for something he said earlier. The first part of the ברייתא is setting up the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "דותה תטמא" in the פסוק about a woman giving birth seem extra, so the ברייתא learns several things from them. The first is that a man who has relations with her becomes טמא like her. This part is not yet the proof. It shows how the ברייתא reads the phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: "From where do I say it?": introduces a speaker's own source
"As in the days of her sickness she shall be impure" (ויקרא 12:2)
To include: the extra words add a case
The man who has relations with her

phrases.english: Abaye said: From where do I say it?
phrases.notes: He is giving the source for his earlier ruling that her days of birth-impurity do not count toward her seven clean days.

phrases.english: As it is taught: "Her sickness she shall be impure" —
to include the one who has relations with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the צריכותא back to אביי's earlier ruling and begins his ברייתא source.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that a woman's days of birth-impurity do not count toward a זבה's שבעה נקיים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that learns from the words "דותה תטמא" (ויקרא 12:2)

steps.title: The ברייתא includes nights and a woman who gives birth while a זבה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the phrase twice more. She is טמאה at night too, and a woman who gives birth while a זבה must sit שבעה נקיים. אביי builds his proof on this last teaching in the next step.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Her sickness she shall be impure" includes the nights. "Her sickness she shall be impure" includes a woman who gives birth while a זבה, teaching that she must sit seven clean days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list. אביי will use the last item, that a woman who gives birth while a זבה must sit שבעה נקיים, as the base for his proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "as in the days," but the ברייתא includes the nights as well. The key addition is the יולדת בזוב: she must still count seven clean days. The ברייתא does not say clean from what, and the next step uses exactly that gap for אביי's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The nights: she is טמאה at night as well as by day
A woman who gives birth while she is a זבה
Seven clean days a זבה must count before becoming טהורה

steps.whatToRemember: From "דותה תטמא" the ברייתא learns three things: her בועל is טמא, she is טמאה at night too, and a יולדת בזוב must count שבעה נקיים. אביי tries to prove his point from the last one.
steps.whyThisMatters: Everyone agrees she must count seven clean days. The argument in the next steps is whether her birth-impurity days can be part of that count.

phrases.english: "Her sickness she shall be impure" — to include the nights,
"Her sickness she shall be impure" — to include a woman who gives birth as a zava,
that she must sit seven clean days.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּוֹתָהּ תִּטְמָא לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַיּוֹלֶדֶת בְּזוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 3 and reaches the part that proves אביי's point.
steps.raayaObject: A woman's days of birth-impurity do not count toward a זבה's שבעה נקיים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The third teaching of the ברייתא learned from "דותה תטמא"

steps.title: אביי reads 'clean days' as clean from the birth
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the ברייתא's requirement of שבעה נקיים means seven days clean from the birth, so the birth-impurity days cannot count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't this mean seven days that are clean from the birth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's proof from the ברייתא. A woman who gives birth while a זבה needs seven clean days, and אביי reads that as seven days after her birth-impurity is over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only said she must sit שבעה נקיים, without saying clean from what. אביי reads 'clean' as clean from the birth itself. That would mean her days of birth-impurity cannot be part of her count.

keyTerms.meaning: Clean days: the seven days a זבה counts without seeing blood
Giving birth, which brings its own period of impurity
'Doesn't it mean...?': a way of offering a reading of a source as a proof

phrases.english: What, is it not clean days from the birth?
phrases.notes: He means: the seven clean days must come after her birth-impurity is finished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the last teaching of the ברייתא from Step 4 proves אביי's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that birth-impurity days do not count toward a זבה's seven clean days
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: a woman who gives birth while a זבה must sit שבעה נקיים

steps.title: Rejected: clean days means clean of blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof: 'clean' means days with no bleeding, and birth-impurity days without blood can still count.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means clean from blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects אביי's reading. The ברייתא could simply mean seven days with no blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'clean' means clean of blood, then her birth-impurity days can count as long as she does not bleed during them. That fits רבא's view, so the ברייתא no longer proves אביי's point.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood; here, actually seeing bleeding
'No': the signal that a proposed proof is being rejected

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not being thrown out. Both sides agree she needs seven clean days. They only argue about what 'clean' means: clean from the birth, or just clean from blood.

phrases.english: No, clean from blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading offered in Step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The ברייתא still stands but is read differently.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'נקיים' can mean clean of blood, not clean of the birth.

steps.title: אביי's second proof: birth days compared to נדה days
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a ברייתא that compares the days of birth to the days of נדה. Neither kind of day can make her a זבה, so neither counts toward the seven clean days.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: How do I know this? A ברייתא teaches: 'Like the days of her נדה', so are the days of her birth. The days of נדה cannot make her a זבה, and the count of seven does not include them. So too, the days of birth cannot make her a זבה, and the count of seven does not include them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new source for his ruling. This ברייתא says outright that birth days do not count toward the seven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא builds a comparison. Blood seen during נדה days cannot make a woman a זבה, and those days don't count toward her seven. Birth days are the same: they cannot make her a זבה, so they don't count either. This proof is stronger than the first, because the ruling is stated directly.

keyTerms.meaning: Her seven days of נדה (monthly) impurity
The status of being a זבה, from bleeding outside the normal נדה days
Fit for זיבה: days on which bleeding could make her a זבה
The count of seven clean days a זבה needs

steps.whyThisMatters: Unlike the first proof, this ברייתא states the ruling directly. So רבא cannot just reread it. He has to answer it a different way, which he does in the next step.

phrases.english: And אביי said: From where do I say it?
As it is taught: 'Like the days of her נדה'
phrases.notes: This phrase is from the section about a woman who gives birth, ויקרא 12.

phrases.english: so are the days of her giving birth.

phrases.aramaic: מָה יְמֵי נִדָּתָהּ אֵין רְאוּיִן לְזִיבָה
phrases.english: Just as the days of her נדה are not fit for זיבה
and the count of seven does not include them,

phrases.aramaic: אַף יְמֵי לֵידָתָהּ שֶׁאֵין רְאוּיִן לְזִיבָה —
phrases.english: so too the days of her giving birth, which are not fit for זיבה,
the count of seven does not include them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was pushed off in Step 6, אביי brings a second, clearer source.
steps.raayaObject: Birth-impurity days do not count toward a זבה's seven clean days
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא comparing birth days to נדה days, built on 'כימי נדתה'

steps.title: רבא: this ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who holds that birth even cancels days already counted. רבא does not follow that view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא? Whose view is this? It is רבי אליעזר, who said that the birth even cancels what was counted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבא deals with אביי's second proof. He says the ברייתא is only one תנא's opinion, רבי אליעזר's, and he does not follow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds a very strict view: birth does not just fail to count, it erases the clean days she had already counted. The ברייתא matches his view. Since רבא follows the other side of that argument, the ברייתא does not bind him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whose view is this?': a way of tying a source to one specific sage
It actually cancels: the birth wipes out clean days already counted
Also, even

phrases.english: And רבא: whose view is this?
phrases.notes: He means: how would רבא answer this ברייתא? He would ask whose opinion it is.

phrases.english: It is רבי אליעזר,
who said: it even cancels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's answer to the ברייתא אביי brought in Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only works according to one תנא, so it does not bind רבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר's strict view, which is not the only opinion.

steps.title: Can we learn the possible from the impossible?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's comparison. A woman cannot be a זבה during her נדה days, but she can give birth while a זבה. So how can the two be compared?
steps.simpleTranslation: But do we learn something possible from something impossible?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the logic of the ברייתא itself. The next steps answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman cannot be a זבה and in her נדה days at the same time. That case is 'impossible', so of course נדה days cannot count toward her seven. But giving birth while a זבה can happen. You cannot learn a case that can happen from a case that cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: We derive, we learn one case from another
Possible: something that can happen
Impossible: something that cannot happen

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not against רבא. It challenges how the ברייתא itself compares birth days to נדה days.

phrases.english: But do we derive the possible from the impossible?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of Step 7 and challenges its comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's comparison of birth days to נדה days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A זבה cannot also be in her נדה days, but she can give birth while a זבה. A case that cannot happen cannot teach about a case that can.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who learns possible from impossible
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי בר אמי answers that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who allows deriving a possible case from an impossible one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחדבוי בר אמי says: This ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who said we may learn a case that can happen from a case that cannot happen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9 about how birth days and נדה days can be compared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 asked how we can compare the two. A woman can give birth while she is a זבה, but she can never become a זבה during her נדה days. רב אחדבוי בר אמי says רבי אליעזר holds that this difference does not stop a comparison, because one may learn the 'possible' (birth during זיבה) from the 'impossible' (זיבה during נדה days).

keyTerms.meaning: We may learn a case that can happen from a case that cannot happen
Possible: a situation that can actually occur
Impossible: a situation that cannot occur

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'possible' means birth, which can happen during זיבה. 'Impossible' means the נדה days, when זיבה cannot happen. Do not mix up which one is which.

phrases.english: Rav Achadvoi bar Ami says:
It follows Rabbi Eliezer,
who said one may derive the possible from the impossible.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא, דְּאָמַר דָּנִין אֶפְשָׁר מִשֶּׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by putting the ברייתא in line with a specific תנא's rule of learning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a תנא who accepts this kind of comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We cannot compare a case that can happen during זיבה to one that cannot.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי אליעזר such a comparison is allowed, so the ברייתא is following his view.

steps.title: The verse itself compared birth days to נדה days
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the תורה placed the two side by side, so the comparison holds no matter what.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת says: Like it or not, the verse compared them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a second answer to the question of step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת does not need רבי אליעזר's rule. Since the פסוק itself links birth impurity to נדה impurity, we must compare them even though one is 'possible' and the other 'impossible'. A comparison made by the verse is followed even where ordinary reasoning would not allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: Like it or not; necessarily
A comparison the תורה makes by placing two things together
The verse

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a comparison taught by the verse is stronger than a regular comparison based on reasoning. So the ברייתא can work even for those who disagree with רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet says:
Perforce the verse juxtaposed them.
phrases.notes: The פסוק is ויקרא 12:2, 'כימי נדת דותה תטמא', which compares a woman after birth to the days of נדה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from step 10, based on the verse's comparison instead of a תנא's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse's direct comparison overrides the logical problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison fails because one case is possible and the other impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse linked them directly, so we must compare them anyway.

steps.title: A second version of who said each answer
steps.stepSummary: Another version gives the first answer to רב אחדבוי בר אמי quoting רב ששת, and the second answer to רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב אחדבוי בר אמי said in the name of רב ששת: It follows רבי אליעזר, who said one may learn the possible from the impossible. And רב פפא says: Like it or not, the verse compared them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the same two answers but changes who said them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ideas stay the same. Only the names change. In this version רב ששת holds the רבי אליעזר answer, and רב פפא is the one who relies on the verse's comparison.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Achadvoi bar Ami says that Rav Sheshet says:
It follows Rabbi Eliezer,
who said one may derive the possible from the impossible.
And Rav Pappa says:
Perforce the verse juxtaposed them.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to save the ברייתא: (1) it follows רבי אליעזר's rule that we may learn possible from impossible, or (2) the verse itself forces the comparison. The two versions only disagree about who said which answer.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates steps 10 and 11 with different names.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different attribution of the same answers
steps.terutzMaskana: Same two answers: רבי אליעזר's rule, or the verse's comparison.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: labor pains for three days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a woman who had labor pains for three days, to discuss it next.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If she had labor pains for three days, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught a case. A woman had labor pains with bleeding during the days of זיבה. Then the pains stopped for 24 hours, and then she gave birth. In that case she is a זבה, because the break shows the blood was not from the birth.

keyTerms.meaning: She had a hard labor; she had labor pains
A woman who gives birth while she is a זבה

phrases.english: If she had labor pains for three days, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the earlier discussion and returns to the text of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the labor pains stopped for 24 hours before the birth, the earlier bleeding counts as זיבה.

steps.title: What if both the pain and the bleeding stopped?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask about a woman whose labor pains and bleeding both stopped before the birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: If she had a break from both this and that, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about a case the משנה did not spell out. Both the pains and the blood stopped for a day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case seems to be one where only the pains stopped and the blood kept flowing. Now we ask about a break from both. Does the stop in the pain still show the blood was not from the birth? Or does the blood stopping together with the pain show they belonged together?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
She had a break; she rested (from pain or bleeding)
What is the law?

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
If she rested from this and from that, what is the law?
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means the labor pains and the bleeding.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: שָׁפְתָה מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a case one step beyond the משנה's case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a 24-hour break from both pain and blood makes her a זבה.

steps.title: רב חסדא says טמאה, רבי חנינא says טהורה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules she is impure as a זבה. רבי חנינא rules she is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא says: She is impure. רבי חנינא says: She is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question and disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא looks at the break in the pain. Since the pains stopped, the blood was not from the birth, so she is a זבה. רבי חנינא looks at the blood stopping together with the pains. That shows the blood belonged to the birth, so she is not a זבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure: here, she is a זבה
Pure: the blood is from the birth, so she is not a זבה

phrases.english: Rav Chisda says: She is impure,
Rabbi Chanina says: She is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: טְמֵאָה, רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: טְהוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposite answers to the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A dispute: רב חסדא says impure, רבי חנינא says pure.

steps.title: רבי חנינא's parable of the king's soldiers
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא compares the blood to soldiers marching ahead of a king: they clearly belong to the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: It is like a king who went out with his soldiers marching ahead of him. Everyone knows they are the king's soldiers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא supports his ruling that she is pure by giving a parable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The birth is the 'king' and the blood is the 'soldiers' that come before it. The blood came before the birth, and there was even a gap, but it still clearly belongs to the birth. So it is birth blood and not זיבה blood.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable; a comparison story
His soldiers; his troops
It is known; it is obvious

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina says:
A parable: to a king who went out,
and his soldiers were ahead of him —
it is known that they are the king's soldiers.
phrases.notes: The king stands for the birth, and the soldiers stand for the blood that came before it.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא: blood that comes before a birth belongs to the birth, like soldiers who march ahead of their king. So if both the pain and the blood stopped, she is טהורה.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי חנינא's ruling in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's ruling that the woman is טהורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A parable: soldiers marching ahead of a king are known to be his

steps.title: רב חסדא turns the soldiers parable around
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא argues that as the king gets closer, the soldiers should get more numerous, not stop. So if the pains and bleeding stopped, the earlier blood was not part of the birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא says: All the more so, there should be many more soldiers.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers רבי חנינא's parable with the same parable, but reads it to support his own view that she is a זבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא said the blood is like soldiers marching ahead of the king, so it belongs to the birth. רב חסדא says that if those were really the king's soldiers, there should be even more of them as the king arrives. A stop before the birth shows they were not his soldiers at all, so the blood was not birth blood.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so
Soldiers (here a picture for the blood and pains before birth)
Many, numerous
More

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda says:
All the more so, there must be
many more soldiers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same parable from Step 16 to reach the opposite conclusion.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's ruling that she is impure as a זבה
steps.raayaSupportSource: Reasoning from the king-and-soldiers parable: real escorts grow as the king nears, they do not stop.

steps.title: Challenge to רב חסדא from רבי יהושע in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says she is a זבה when she rested from the pain but not from the blood. That suggests that if both stopped, she is pure, which goes against רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: רבי יהושע says: a night and a day, like the night of שבת and its day, where she rested from the pain but not from the blood. The reason is that it was from the pain and not from the blood. But from both, she is pure. This is a refutation of רב חסדא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the exact wording of רבי יהושע in the משנה and draws an inference that seems to disprove רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע describes the זבה case as one where only the pain stopped, while the blood kept coming. The גמרא infers that if both pain and blood stopped, she would be pure. But רב חסדא said that in exactly that case she is impure.

keyTerms.meaning: She rested, had a break (from labor)
Pain (here, labor pains)
The reason is X; this implies that otherwise... (an inference from wording)
A strong refutation

phrases.english: We learned: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
a night and a day, like the night of Shabbat and its day,
where she rested from the pain
but not from the blood.

phrases.aramaic: טַעְמָא דְּמִן הַצַּעַר וְלֹא מִן הַדָּם,
phrases.english: The reason is that she rested from the pain and not from the blood,
but if from this and that, she is pure.
This is a refutation of Rav Chisda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's position from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that a woman whose pains and bleeding both stopped is a זבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says she is a זבה when only the pain stopped. That implies that when both stopped she is pure, which contradicts רב חסדא.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the משנה teaches the bigger new point
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that when both stopped, it is obvious she is a זבה. The משנה chose the harder case, where blood kept coming, to teach that even then she is a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא can say to you: It is not needed to teach that if both stopped she is impure, since the soldiers stopped completely. But when the pain stopped and not the blood, I might say: just as she did not stop bleeding, she also did not stop laboring, and she is just in a daze. So the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains why the משנה mentioned only the case where the pain stopped. It is not because the case where both stopped is pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both pain and blood stopped, it is clear the 'soldiers' are gone, so she is obviously a זבה. The harder case is when the blood keeps coming, because we might think she is still in labor and only feels no pain because she is dazed and weak. The משנה teaches that even there, she is a זבה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed to say (this case is obvious)
A daze, a state of confusion or weakness
Labor pains, hard labor
This teaches us (a new point)

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה mentions the harder case, not the easier one. Mentioning only one case does not mean the other case gets the opposite ruling. Here the unmentioned case (both stopped) is even more clearly impure.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda can say to you:
It is not needed to teach that from this and that she is impure,
since the soldiers have stopped completely,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִן הַצַּעַר וְלֹא מִן הַדָּם,
phrases.english: but when it is from the pain and not from the blood,

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּמִדָּם לָא פָּסְקָה,
phrases.english: I might say: just as she did not stop from blood,
she also did not stop from labor,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא תּוּנְבָּא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא דִּנְקַט לַהּ,
phrases.english: and it is just a daze that has taken hold of her,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב חִסְדָּא: לָא מִבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב חסדא against the challenge in Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: לא מיבעיא: the משנה states the bigger new point, and the unmentioned case is even more obvious
steps.terutzHavaAmina: When the blood keeps flowing, we might think she is still in labor and just too dazed to feel the pain, so she would be pure.
steps.terutzMaskana: A stop from both obviously makes her a זבה. The משנה teaches that even when the blood continues, a stop in pain makes her a זבה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic way of reading a משנה: it often states the harder case, and the easier case is understood without being said.

steps.title: Setting up a challenge to רבי חנינא from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the case in the משנה: a woman had labor pains three days during the eleven days, rested for 24 hours, then gave birth. She is called one who gives birth as a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: If she had labor pains for three days within the eleven days, and rested for a full day, and then gave birth, she is one who gives birth as a זבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to challenge רבי חנינא, who said she is pure. It quotes this line of the משנה to set up the challenge, which will be developed next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that a 24-hour break before the birth makes her a זבה. רבי חנינא only said she is pure when both the pain and the blood stopped, so the challenge depends on how this case is read. The next lines work that out.

keyTerms.meaning: She had hard labor, labor pains
The eleven days between periods, when bleeding can make a woman a זבה
A full 24-hour period
A woman who gives birth while a זבה

phrases.english: We learned: If she had labor pains for three days
within the eleven days,
and she rested for a full day, and she gave birth,
this woman is one who gives birth as a zavah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: קִשְּׁתָה שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים בְּתוֹךְ אַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב חסדא, the גמרא turns to challenge the other side, רבי חנינא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's ruling that a woman whose pains and bleeding stopped before birth is pure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה calls a woman who rested 24 hours before giving birth a זבה. This seems to go against רבי חנינא; the exact inference follows next.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need three days of pain?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה means she stopped having pain but kept bleeding, the number 'three days' of pain looks unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: What exactly is the case? If it is just as the משנה says (the pain stopped but the blood kept coming), why do I need three days? Two days with pain and one day of rest should be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how to picture the משנה's case. It points out that reading the משנה as 'pain stopped, blood continued' makes the words 'three days of pain' seem pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the simple reading, the day she rested from pain but still bled already counts toward making her a זבה. So two days of pain plus one day of resting with blood should be enough. The extra third day of pain looks like a wasted detail, which pushes the גמרא to look for a different reading.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?
If you say
As it is taught, just as the words say
Labor pain, hard labor
Rest, ease from the pain
It is enough

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say it is just as it is taught,
phrases.notes: He means: she rested from the pain but the bleeding kept going, the reading from step 18.

phrases.english: why do I need three days?
With two days in labor pain
and one day at rest, it would be enough!

steps.triggerLanguage: היכי דמי? אילימא כדקתני, למה לי שלש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the משנה case quoted in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of the משנה, where the pain stopped but the blood continued
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, the 'three days of pain' would be an unneeded detail, since two days of pain plus one day of resting with blood is already enough.

steps.title: A new reading of the משנה refutes רבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה as two cases, and the first case shows that blood seen during pains that later stopped is not birth blood. That goes against רבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't this what the משנה means: she had pains for three days and then rested from both the pain and the blood, or she had pains for two days and then rested from the pain for twenty-four hours. Either way she gives birth as a זבה. That is a refutation of רבי חנינא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the משנה really describes two cases. It then uses the first case to attack רבי חנינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, she bled during three days of pain, and then both the pain and the bleeding stopped. She is still a זבה, so the blood from those pain days was not birth blood. This contradicts רבי חנינא's 'soldiers before the king' idea from step 16, that blood during pain belongs to the birth.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that
From this and from that, meaning from both pain and blood
A full twenty-four-hour period
A woman who gives birth while she is a זבה
A strong refutation

phrases.english: Rather, is this not what it is saying:
she had labor pains for three days,
and she rested from both this and that,
phrases.notes: Both the pain and the bleeding stopped.

phrases.english: or she had labor pains for two days,
and she rested for twenty-four hours,
this woman gives birth as a zava,
and that is a refutation of Rabbi Chanina!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the reading that the question in step 21 seemed to force, and uses it against רבי חנינא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's view that blood seen during labor pains belongs to the birth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she bled during three days of pain and then everything stopped, and she is still a זבה, then blood during pain is not automatically birth blood.

steps.title: The משנה is aimed at a different רבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא keeps the simple reading. He explains that the three days teach that pain beginning on the third day does not help, and that this point argues against a different sage with the same name.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא can tell you: No. The משנה really means just what it says. It is teaching us that even if the pain began on the third day, and she then rested for twenty-four hours, she is impure. This rules out the view of רבי חנינא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא defends himself. He says the משנה should be read as written, and the 'three days' detail has a purpose of its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions three days to show that even if the pain started on the third day of bleeding, she is still a זבה once the pain stops for twenty-four hours. That point rejects another sage's view (from 36b), who says pain on part of the third day saves her. So the משנה is not about our רבי חנינא's 'soldiers' idea at all, and he is not refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in fact (used to keep the original reading)
This is what it teaches us
Even though
Impure
To exclude, to reject a certain opinion

steps.confusionAlert: The name רבי חנינא appears twice here, but these are two different sages. The first one (the speaker) is the 'soldiers before the king' רבי חנינא. The one being excluded is the sage from 36b who holds that pain on part of the third day helps.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina can say to you:
No, really it is just as it is taught,
and this is what it teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּמַתְחֵיל קִישּׁוּי בַּשְּׁלִישִׁי,
phrases.english: that even though the labor pain began on the third day,
and she rested for twenty-four hours,
she is impure,
to exclude the view of Rabbi Chanina.
phrases.notes: This is a different sage, the one from 36b who says pain on part of the third day saves her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation in step 22 by keeping the simple reading and giving the 'three days' a different purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the purpose of the detail in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'three days' seemed pointless, so the משנה had to be read as including a case where both pain and blood stopped, which refutes רבי חנינא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'three days' teaches that pain starting on the third day does not help. This argues against a different sage, so our רבי חנינא stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'three days' can be read as written. It rejects the view that pain on the third day saves her, and it does not disprove the 'soldiers before the king' idea.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: how early can labor pains start?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, which asks how long before birth labor pains can count, and cites רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: How long can her labor pains last? רבי מאיר says, and so on (even forty or fifty days).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה. This is a setup for the question that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה asks how many days before the birth pain can still be counted as labor pain, so that the blood is not counted as זיבה. רבי מאיר gives two numbers, forty and fifty days, and the next step asks about that.

keyTerms.meaning: Her labor pains (the period of hard labor)
And so on, the rest of the quote

phrases.english: How long is her labor pain?
Rabbi Meir says, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: כמה היא קשויה? רבי מאיר אומר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, labor pains can begin as much as forty or fifty days before birth.

steps.title: Why mention forty if fifty is already true?
steps.stepSummary: If pains can start fifty days before birth, it seems pointless to also say forty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if she can have labor pains fifty days before, do we need to be told forty?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. Saying both numbers looks repetitive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fifty days is the bigger number. If pain fifty days before birth counts as labor, then pain forty days before surely counts too. So why mention forty at all?

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since (used to say 'if the bigger case is true')
Is it necessary to say?

phrases.english: Now, if she can have labor pains fifty days before,
is it necessary to say forty?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the משנה quoted in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's mention of both forty and fifty days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The larger number already includes the smaller one, so mentioning forty seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Sick woman versus healthy woman
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the two numbers are for two different women: fifty days for a sick woman and forty for a healthy one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is not a problem. One number is for a sick woman, and the other is for a healthy woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by saying the two numbers are not repetitive. Each one applies to a different kind of woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sick woman can have labor pains much earlier, up to fifty days before birth. A healthy woman can have them only up to forty days before. So each number has its own job, and neither one is wasted.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, there is no problem
Here... here (this case... that case)
A sick woman
A healthy woman

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, pain fifty days before birth can count as labor for a sick woman, and pain forty days before birth for a healthy woman.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: It is not difficult.
Here, it is for a sick woman;
phrases.notes: This goes with the fifty days.

phrases.english: there, it is for a healthy woman.
phrases.notes: This goes with the forty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב חסדא: לא קשיא — כאן לחולה, כאן לבריאה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two numbers between two different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forty and fifty seemed to describe the same woman, which would make one of the numbers repetitive.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fifty days is for a sick woman, and forty days is for a healthy woman.

steps.title: רבי לוי limits when the birth keeps the mother pure
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי rules that the birth keeps the mother from becoming a זבה only on the days when a woman can become a זבה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: The child makes the mother pure only on the days that are fit for her to become a זבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רבי לוי sets a limit on the rule that labor-pain blood does not make a woman a זבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman can only become a זבה if she sees blood on certain days, the days outside her נדה time. רבי לוי says the birth 'purifies' her only on those days. In other words, the birth can only save her from זיבה on days when זיבה was possible to begin with.

keyTerms.meaning: The child, meaning the birth of the baby
Makes pure. Here it means the birth keeps her from becoming a זבה
A woman who sees blood outside her normal נדה time and becomes impure in a special way
Days that are fit or able, meaning days on which something can happen

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the outer edge of the labor-pain rule. רב is about to argue with this limit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:
The child does not make pure
phrases.notes: He means the birth keeps the blood seen during labor from counting as זיבה blood.

phrases.english: except on days that are fit
for her to become a zava on them,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: אֵין הַוָּלָד מְטַהֵר אֶלָּא יָמִים הָרְאוּיִין לִהְיוֹת בָּהֶן זָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about how far the labor-pain rule reaches, after the steps about the משנה's time limits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The birth keeps the mother from becoming a זבה only on days when she could become a זבה.

steps.title: רב extends the rule to the counting days of a zava
steps.stepSummary: רב disagrees and says the birth also keeps her pure on the days fit for a זבה's counting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב said: Even on the days that are fit for the counting of a זבה, the birth keeps her pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the other side of the מחלוקת. He says the rule covers more days than רבי לוי allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי לוי allowed only the days on which a woman can become a זבה. רב adds the days on which a זבה would count her clean days. So by רב, the birth helps on a wider set of days.

keyTerms.meaning: The counting of a זבה, the clean days she counts before she can become pure
Even. It shows that רב is adding more days

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of days. 'Days fit to become a זבה' (רבי לוי) are not the same as 'days fit for a זבה's counting' (רב). רב includes both.

phrases.english: And Rav said:
even on days that are fit
for the counting of a zava.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בְּיָמִים הָרְאוּיִין לִסְפִירַת זָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רבי לוי and extends the rule to more days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The birth keeps the mother pure even on days fit for the counting of a זבה.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה begins a conclusion from רב's view
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה begins to point out something that follows from רב's reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: And according to רב's reasoning...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רב אדא בר אהבה is getting ready to show what follows if we accept רב's view, and his point continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'according to his reasoning' tells us a new result is coming from רב's wider rule. We do not yet know whether the result will be a new law or a difficulty for רב. That becomes clear only in the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his reasoning, following his own logic
Reason, the logic behind a ruling

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
And according to the reasoning of Rav,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב's ruling in step 28 to draw out what it leads to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces a conclusion that follows from רב's view. The content continues in the next lines.
